term:Security Testing.deep_dive: Probing AI systems for exploitable weaknesses — conventional (access, injection, infrastructure) plus ML-specific: can training data be poisoned, can the model be inverted or stolen, do adversarial inputs flip outputs, do prompts jailbreak it. Red teaming is its adversarial, exercise-style form.
term:Security Testing.exam_tip: Match attack to test: poisoning (training-time), inversion/membership (privacy), adversarial examples (inference-time), injection (LLM) — coverage questions expect the full family.

term:Stress Testing (AI).deep_dive: Pushing the system past comfortable conditions before launch: peak loads, degraded infrastructure, malformed inputs, adversarial prompts, edge-case scenarios — measuring latency, resource ceilings, failover behavior, and failure gracefulness. The readiness gate's empirical core.
term:Stress Testing (AI).exam_tip: Stress testing = operational limits and failure behavior — complementary to accuracy validation, not a substitute.

term:STRIDE.deep_dive: Microsoft's threat-modeling mnemonic — Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege — applied to AI pipelines: tampering maps to data poisoning, information disclosure to model inversion, DoS to resource-exhaustion attacks on inference.
term:STRIDE.exam_tip: STRIDE = threat modeling framework (security analysis structure), not an AI-specific control — recognize and map its categories.

term:System Card.deep_dive: Documentation for the deployed whole: the assembled system's components, data flows, model interactions, oversight points, and operational context — one level up from model cards, because users experience systems, not models, and risk lives in the assembly.
term:System Card.exam_tip: Model card documents the model; system card documents the assembled deployment — pick the right artifact for the scope.

term:Test Data (Evaluation Data).deep_dive: The held-out final exam: data untouched during training and tuning, used once to estimate real-world performance honestly. Its integrity is sacred — leakage from training, or repeated tuning against it, silently converts 'evaluation' into fiction.
term:Test Data (Evaluation Data).exam_tip: Train fits, validation tunes, test evaluates — and tuning on test data is the invalidation pattern to spot.

term:Training and Testing.deep_dive: The paired disciplines of the model lifecycle: learn from training data, then verify against data the model never saw — with the discipline being separation. The phrase names the workflow whose corruption (leakage, test-set tuning) invalidates every quality claim downstream.
term:Training and Testing.exam_tip: The separation is the point — any scenario blending training and evaluation data is describing invalidated results.

term:Transparency (System).deep_dive: The system-level property: information about a specific system's capabilities, limitations, data, and logic is available to those who need it — the substrate for informed use, effective oversight, and contestable decisions. Companion to explainability: transparency supplies information, explainability makes outputs comprehensible.
term:Transparency (System).exam_tip: Transparency = information availability; explainability = output comprehensibility — the exam's favorite near-synonym split.

term:Underfitting.deep_dive: The model that never learned: too simple, too constrained, or too starved to capture real patterns — performing poorly on training data and new data alike. Remedies run opposite to overfitting's: more capacity, richer features, longer training.
term:Underfitting.exam_tip: Bad everywhere = underfitting; great on training only = overfitting — the diagnostic pair in one line.

term:Unit Testing.deep_dive: Testing components in isolation — a preprocessing function, a feature transform, a scoring module — before integration compounds failures. In ML pipelines it covers the deterministic scaffolding around the model; the model itself needs statistical evaluation beyond pass/fail assertions.
term:Unit Testing.exam_tip: Unit tests verify pipeline components; model quality needs validation testing — the ladder starts here but can't end here.

term:Use Case.deep_dive: The defined application: what the system does, for whom, in what context, with what success criteria — the unit governance attaches to. Risk classification, impact assessment, and approval all bind to the use case, which is why undocumented new uses are governance violations, not features.
term:Use Case.exam_tip: Approvals attach to use cases, not models — same model, new use case, new assessment.

term:Use Case Assessment.deep_dive: The screening gate for proposed AI applications: value, feasibility, data availability, risk profile, and regulatory exposure evaluated before commitment — where bad ideas die cheap and good ideas acquire their governance requirements. The first formal artifact in a well-run lifecycle.
term:Use Case Assessment.exam_tip: Sequencing: assess the use case before collecting data or building — the earliest and cheapest control gate.

term:Vendor Agreement.deep_dive: The contract that allocates AI risk between customer and supplier: data-use limits, performance and bias warranties, audit rights, model-change and incident notification, IP and confidentiality terms, liability, and exit portability. For AI vendors it's where governance requirements become enforceable obligations.
term:Vendor Agreement.exam_tip: The AI-specific clauses (data use, bias warranties, change notice, audit rights) are what distinguish an adequate AI vendor agreement from a generic one.

term:Workforce Readiness.deep_dive: Whether the organization's people are prepared for AI — skills to build and govern it, literacy to use it appropriately, and change management for the roles it transforms. A readiness gap is a deployment risk in its own right: capable systems operated by unprepared workforces produce incidents.
term:Workforce Readiness.exam_tip: Readiness assessments include the humans — technology-ready but workforce-unready is a failing state the exam recognizes.
